looks.note: Three close stone tones share the interface: the lightest for the page, the middle one for panels, the darkest for a single band, all with charcoal type. Saturated colour is left to the photographs and their backdrops; the grey-green fills the button only.

looks.name: Putty and black
looks.note: Warm putty covers the page and pure black handles all type and the main shapes. The only tint in the interface is teal, used for the one button or a single marker placed near the photographs.

looks.name: Sand and moss
looks.note: Sand grey holds the page with charcoal type, and one deep leaf-green band may close it. Moss green is reserved for buttons; brighter greens and blues arrive only through photographs.

looks.name: Bone, green, chocolate
looks.note: Bone ground with chocolate-brown text takes most of the page. The green is spent on one large flat block, about a third of a screen, and on the button; all other colour comes from photographs.

looks.name: Lunar and bronze
looks.note: Soft black holds the page with panels one step lighter, white text and grey secondary lines, so photographs supply all the colour. Muted bronze goes on small markers and the one button only.

looks.name: Night and sky blue
looks.note: Blue-black ground and slate panels with silver-white text fill the page; no section changes colour. A sky blue marks the buttons and the links, nothing else.

looks.name: Green-black and bone
looks.note: Bone type on green-black from top to bottom, with panels and drawn details barely lighter than the ground so photographs supply the colour. Pale jade is for the booking or contact button alone.

looks.name: Black and crimson
looks.note: Black with off-white text and mid-grey texture takes nearly the whole page, and the last sections may invert to off-white with black type. Deep crimson is scattered sparingly: a few characters in a heading, a slider fill, the one button.

looks.name: Forest and lime
looks.note: Forest green, black and white sections alternate, with forest green holding the most; photographs stay in moss greens and stone browns. Pale lime sits on small squares only, such as arrow buttons and the closing wordmark.

looks.name: Charcoal and sage
looks.note: Charcoal holds the page with off-white text, and one section may flip to a pale concrete tone with dark text. Colour comes from the photographs; grey sage is used for the single button and the active state of a control.

looks.name: Warm black, gold
looks.note: Warm near-black fills the page and photographs sit bright against it, with pure white small type; panels warm to a brown-black. Gold is for one text link or small button per screen, never a field.

looks.name: Graphite and orange
looks.note: Graphite and cool light-grey sections alternate, graphite taking about two thirds, and photographs are chosen calm and low in colour so nothing competes (in full colour where the pictures carry the colour; greyscale only where section 0 deals black-and-white). Safety orange marks the buttons, one thick solid bar across the top of the page and the highlighted item in a list or chart.

looks.name: Soot and lime
looks.note: A soot-black opening and close bracket white middle sections, all in black, white and grey. Pale lime is the single action colour: every button, and at most one headline set in it on the dark ground.

looks.name: Plum-black and pink
looks.note: Near-black and plum at the top and bottom bracket a white middle with navy-black text. Hot pink is reserved for primary buttons, bars in charts and map markers; it never fills a section.

looks.name: Signal red, white
looks.note: White ground, black text and paper grey for filled panels, with one full black band allowed. Signal red is the only colour in the interface: the button and a few solid blocks, never a word in a headline.

looks.name: Greys and mint
looks.note: White, near-black and two greys fill a board of flat tiles. Mint floods a few whole tiles (one statement, one figure, the closing call to action) and appears nowhere else.

looks.name: Bottle ink, yellow
looks.note: Off-white ground with all type in a near-black bottle green instead of black. Yellow is the only saturated note: the button or one small object on most screens, and one later section that turns fully yellow.

looks.name: Teal on paper
looks.note: Cool white paper and a single teal used for every word, shape and button, with no black anywhere. The accent is that same teal filled solid, for the button and for one inverted band with paper-coloured type.

looks.name: Navy and pink
looks.note: One navy field runs the entire page. Pink does everything else, from the name and headings to body text, and fills one solid button.

looks.name: Blush and aubergine
looks.note: Blush pink and dark aubergine alternate as full fields and serve as each other's text colour, in roughly equal shares. There is no third colour: the button is a solid block of whichever of the two is not the ground.

looks.name: Cobalt on sand
looks.note: Sand paper and one cobalt do everything: text, drawings and solid shapes are all the same blue. The button is a cobalt block with sand-coloured type, and no black or second hue is used.

looks.name: Oxblood and grey
looks.note: Deep red text on grey paper holds most of the page, then pale grey text on a solid red field takes one long section and the footer. Photographs are chosen calm and low in colour so nothing breaks the pair (in full colour where the pictures carry the colour; greyscale only where section 0 deals black-and-white), and the button is a solid red block.

looks.name: Olive on bone
looks.note: A bone page with every word, large or small, in one olive green; the footer inverts to a solid olive field with bone text. Photography supplies all other colour, and the button is the same olive, filled.

looks.name: Burgundy and bubblegum
looks.note: Deep burgundy is the ground for the whole page and bubblegum pink sets every word on it. The button and the active state of a control are solid pink with burgundy type; product photographs supply any other colour.

looks.name: Bottle green, gold
looks.note: Bottle green covers the page and warm gold sets all the type, with panels one step lighter than the ground. The button is solid gold with green text, and photographs are kept dark and warm so the pair is not disturbed.

looks.name: Cobalt field
looks.note: One electric cobalt fills everything, with white and pale type; photographs keep their own colour and are shown large. A single yellow dot or button is the only other colour on the page.

looks.name: Mustard and black
looks.note: One warm mustard field for the whole page with black ink only. Royal blue is the single interruption, kept to a sliver along one edge or one small button.

looks.name: Carmine field
looks.note: A deep red field bookends or fills the page, with white type and pale pink secondary lines; work shown in between sits on flat charcoal so it keeps its own colours. The button is a pale pink block with red type.

looks.name: Bubblegum and lime
looks.note: A flat bubblegum pink field with black type from top to bottom. Fluorescent lime is the action colour only: the menu button, one highlighter swipe behind a word and the main button.

looks.note: Sky blue sits behind everything, white cards lie on top of it, and navy handles all text and the footer. Orange is for buttons and one highlighted word, so orange against blue is the single clash on the page.

looks.name: Tobacco and olive
looks.note: Tobacco brown fills the page with bone type, and photographs stay in browns and ochre. One olive block holds the main text or the button, and a single ochre band may break the brown once.

looks.name: Ultramarine and yellow
looks.note: Each section is one flat field in sequence: ultramarine, black, yellow, then ultramarine again, with white type on blue and black, and black type on yellow. Green is the only small accent and never grows larger than a button.

looks.name: Post red, mustard
looks.note: Post red and bone alternate as full section fields, with red holding the opening and the close. Mustard, slate blue and maroon are kept for whole card frames, and slate blue also fills the one button.

looks.name: Grey, mint, orange
looks.note: Black on white to start, then whole sections flood with flat mid-grey, acid mint and orange in turn. Photographs inside a flooded section keep the treatment section 0 deals (black-and-white only where it deals that), and mint is also the button colour on white and black.

looks.note: A white base with flat blocks of orange, sage, acid yellow and black assigned to whole modules: figure tiles, quote panels and chapter bands. Text is black on every colour and off-white on black, and orange is also the button colour.

looks.name: Card pastels
looks.note: Neutral paper ground and black type, with each card or tile given its own flat pastel (sky, lime, amber or cyan), never two alike side by side. Magenta is reserved for the logo, the email address and text links.

looks.name: Mint and pink
looks.note: Near-white base with black type; mint and pink are the only two colours and each stands for one side of the product. They first appear as small circles, then as full-screen section fields, and deep green is used only for the button.

looks.name: Swapping pastels
looks.note: One flat pastel is the whole background and it swaps per project or chapter: pale sky, pink, sand, sage, peach. Type and one solid box stay near-black on all five, and dark teal is only for the button.

looks.name: Blush, sage, slate
looks.note: Slate blue-grey, sage and blush share the page as soft flat blocks, one per chapter or menu tile, with dark type; one deep olive block anchors the close with pale type. Olive is also the button colour, and photographs of sea and sky do the rest.

looks.name: Candy on black
looks.note: Black ground and dark photographs take nearly all of the surface. The only flat colour is a solid block behind each title, which takes a new candy pastel per project (mint, cyan, lemon, orange, sky); cyan is the default for the button.

looks.name: Sky and sand
looks.note: Sky blue and sand yellow are the constant ground, each holding whole sections, with black text throughout. Saturated colour arrives only as small solid objects, and magenta is kept for the contact card and its button.

looks.name: Studio grey
looks.note: One mid grey serves as both page and studio backdrop, so the photographed object seems to stand on the page itself; type is black and one black band comes late. Colour comes only from the product, and racing green is for the single button.

looks.name: Walnut and tan
looks.note: Dark walnut holds the opening and the close with bone type, and the middle of the page may turn to flat tan around honey-lit photographs. There is no bright accent: tan is the fill for the one button on walnut.

looks.name: Warm paper and walnut
looks.note: Warm off-white holds the page with brown-black type and one darker paper step for the visit panel and the goods cards. Walnut brown is the one button, the focus ring and the links; photographs carry the rest of the colour.

looks.name: Flour and terracotta
looks.note: A flour-white ground with warm brown-black type and a sand step for panels. Terracotta red is the main button and the brand band, never a second fill; the photographs of ovens, tiles and bread bring the warmth.

looks.name: Linen and harbour blue
looks.note: Linen white with blue-black type and one greyer linen step for the booking form and the room cards. A muted harbour blue is the one button and the brand band; nothing else is tinted.

looks.name: Limewash and ochre
looks.note: A limewashed off-white with near-black brown type and a straw step for panels. Ochre is the button and the focus ring, darkened so its white label reads; the ground stays quiet under warm photographs.

looks.name: Clay and pine
looks.note: Pale clay holds the page with green-black type and a darker clay step for panels. Pine green is the one button and may fill the brand band at the close; wood, stone and plants in the photographs match it.

looks.name: Chalk and tomato
looks.note: Chalk white with near-black type and one warm step for the menu panel. Tomato red is the order button and the brand band and appears nowhere else; the menu stays black type on the ground.

looks.name: Plaster and rose
looks.note: Pale plaster with warm near-black type and a pinker plaster step for panels. A deep rose is the one button and the brand band; flowers and fabric in the photographs carry the softer colour.

looks.name: Steel and orange
looks.note: Light steel grey with graphite type and one darker grey step for panels and the price rows. Workshop orange is the one button and the focus ring; tools and bikes in the photographs bring their own colour.
